# Generated files

Go2APK writes a set of files that are entirely derived from `go2apk.yaml` and
your Go source. They are rewritten on every build, they are not meant to be read
by humans except when debugging, and they should not be committed.

| Path | Produced by | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `android/` | `init`, `generate`, `build` | The Gradle project: Java sources, manifest, resources, Gradle scripts |
| `scripts/` | `init`, `sdk install` | `build-go-app.sh`, `install-sdk.sh`, `install-sdk.ps1` |
| `preview.html` | `preview` | An HTML approximation of the layout |
| `dist/` | `build`, `release` | The APKs and AABs |
| `<source>/events_gen.go` | `generate`, `build` | Registers your Go event handlers so Java can call them |
| `<source>/jni_exports_gen.go` | `generate`, `build` | The JNI entry points the Android runtime calls into |

## Why generated Go is deleted before every parse

`events_gen.go` and `jni_exports_gen.go` are written **inside the package your
app lives in**. That is deliberate: they have to be compiled into your app.

It also means they would otherwise be parsed as if they were your code. A stale
one from an earlier run — left behind after you renamed a widget, say — can fail
to compile, and then every later `check` or `generate` fails too, because the
tool cannot parse the package it is trying to fix. There is no way out of that
by running the tool again.

So before parsing, Go2APK deletes the Go files it generated previously. It only
deletes files carrying the marker

```go
// Code generated by go2apk. DO NOT EDIT.
```

A file of the same name that you wrote yourself does not carry the marker and is
never touched.

## The `.gitignore` you want

```gitignore
# Go build outputs
/bin/
/dist/

# Generated by go2apk init / go2apk build
/android/app/
/android/build.gradle
/android/settings.gradle
/android/.gradle/
/android/build/
/scripts/

# Generated into the app's source directory on every build
events_gen.go
jni_exports_gen.go

# Generated previews
preview.html

# Local toolchain installs and release keys
.go2apk/
*.jks
*.keystore
```

`go2apk init` writes a `.gitignore` along these lines. If you are adding Go2APK
to an existing repository, copy the block above.

The `android/` directory is a special case: it holds the Go runtime package
(`android/android.go` and friends) that apps import, **and** the generated
Gradle project under `android/app/`. The Go files are part of the repository;
everything under `android/app/` is generated.

## Customising the build

Change `go2apk.yaml`, not the generated files. Every generated file is rewritten
from it, so hand-edits are lost on the next build — and if they are not lost
because the file happens not to be regenerated, you now have a project that
cannot be reproduced from its inputs.

If you need behaviour Go2APK does not generate, that is a missing feature rather
than something to patch into `android/`.
